summary: In this excerpt from a fiction book, the narrator Russell has killed the remaining attackers in a hallway and returns to a doorway with his companion Arthur. Russell stops watching the door and instead pries microchips off a PCI card, following Rio's advice to keep his eyes down. A single set of footsteps then enters the room, and Dawna Polk speaks, saying she won't kill him and is observing him closely.
one_line: Russell, bloodied after killing attackers, pretends to repair a circuit board as Dawna Polk enters the room.
key_facts: The narrator took out the remaining seven attackers in the hallway before returning to the doorway.
The narrator's boots left wet, red footprints behind him.
Arthur held a Beretta at high ready and kept his eyes on the hall.
The narrator had a stolen M4 settled against his shoulder while waiting.
The building stayed quiet for one minute, then two minutes.
The narrator said, "They aren't coming," and went back to the table.
The narrator picked up a PCI card and began prying tiny microchips off it with a utility knife.
Arthur mumbled, "God help me, I maybe believe you."
Only one set of footsteps entered the hallway, one light, quiet set.
Rio had told the narrator to keep his eyes on the circuit board and not to speak.
Dawna Polk entered the room and said, "Good evening."
Dawna Polk said, "You won't kill me."
Dawna Polk told the narrator he was unusually effective at dispatching her people.
Arthur moved back from the doorway as the footsteps entered the room.
